1B1.t: Kefir overnight oats with kiwi & walnuts
1B1.p: Night before: stir the oats and linseed into the kefir and kwark in a jar or box. Cover and refrigerate overnight — the oats soften and the kefir keeps working. Morning: peel and slice the two kiwis over the top, crumble the walnuts on.
s: Night before: stir the oats and linseed into the kefir and kwark in a jar or box.
Cover and refrigerate overnight — the oats soften and the kefir keeps working.
Morning: peel and slice the two kiwis over the top, crumble the walnuts on.
1B1.tip: Kefir carries a wider mix of live bacteria and yeasts than kwark alone; linseed adds soluble fibre, which is usually far better tolerated than the sugars in beans.

1B2.t: Baked syrniki with orange & a glass of kefir
1B2.p: Heat the oven to 200 °C. Line a tray with baking paper, or use a silicone muffin tin (easiest with Dutch kwark). Blitz the oats to a coarse flour, then mix with the kwark and both eggs into a thick batter. Add a pinch of cinnamon. Rest the batter 10 minutes so the oats soak up moisture — magere kwark is wetter than Russian tvorog. Spoon into 6 mounds (or muffin cups), flatten slightly, bake 18–20 minutes until set and golden underneath. Serve warm with the orange segments, and drink the kefir alongside.
s: Heat the oven to 200 °C. Line a tray with baking paper, or use a silicone muffin tin (easiest with Dutch kwark).
Blitz the oats to a coarse flour, then mix with the kwark and both eggs into a thick batter. Add a pinch of cinnamon.
Rest the batter 10 minutes so the oats soak up moisture — magere kwark is wetter than Russian tvorog.
Spoon into 6 mounds (or muffin cups), flatten slightly, bake 18–20 minutes until set and golden underneath.
Serve warm with the orange segments, and drink the kefir alongside.
1B2.tip: The kwark here is baked, so its cultures don't survive — the glass of kefir is what makes this breakfast count as fermented.

1D1.p: Heat the oven to 200 °C. Boil the potatoes 15 minutes. Cut the fennel into wedges, toss with the oil and roast 15–18 minutes. Add the salmon and halved tomatoes to the tray for the last 12–14 minutes. Finish with lemon and black pepper.
s: Heat the oven to 200 °C. Boil the potatoes 15 minutes.
Cut the fennel into wedges, toss with the oil and roast 15–18 minutes.
Add the salmon and halved tomatoes to the tray for the last 12–14 minutes.
Finish with lemon and black pepper.
1D1.tip: Oily fish twice a week covers omega-3; fennel at this amount is gentle — only very large portions trouble sensitive guts.

1D2.t: Tofu & pak choi stir-fry with rice
1D2.p: Press the tofu between two plates with a weight on top for 20 minutes, then cube it. Cook the rice (1:2 water, 25 minutes). Warm the oil with a lightly crushed garlic clove for 2 minutes on low heat, then lift the clove out — the flavour stays in the oil, the gas-forming fructans don't (they are water-soluble, not oil-soluble). Fry the tofu in the hot garlic oil and leave it alone until it colours, 6–8 minutes; lift out. Stir-fry carrot and pepper 3 minutes, pak choi 2 minutes, then return the tofu with grated ginger and a splash of rice vinegar. Serve on the rice with the spring-onion greens.
s: Press the tofu between two plates with a weight on top for 20 minutes, then cube it.
Cook the rice (1:2 water, 25 minutes).

Warm the oil with a lightly crushed garlic clove for 2 minutes on low heat, then lift the clove out — the flavour stays in the oil, the gas-forming fructans don't (they are water-soluble, not oil-soluble).
Fry the tofu in the hot garlic oil and leave it alone until it colours, 6–8 minutes; lift out.
Stir-fry carrot and pepper 3 minutes, pak choi 2 minutes, then return the tofu with grated ginger and a splash of rice vinegar.
Serve on the rice with the spring-onion greens.
1D2.tip: Firm tofu is one of the few legume foods that is low in gas-forming GOS — they drain away with the liquid when the curd is pressed during production.

1D3.t: Chicken thigh traybake with carrots & a dill dip
1D3.p: Heat the oven to 200 °C. Cut the potatoes into wedges, carrots and pepper into chunks, courgette into rounds. Toss vegetables and chicken with the oil, paprika powder and black pepper on one tray; roast 30–35 minutes, turning once. Dip: stir chopped dill, lemon and black pepper into the kwark. Scatter the sliced spring-onion greens over the tray and serve with the cold dip.
s: Heat the oven to 200 °C. Cut the potatoes into wedges, carrots and pepper into chunks, courgette into rounds.
Toss vegetables and chicken with the oil, paprika powder and black pepper on one tray; roast 30–35 minutes, turning once.
Dip: stir chopped dill, lemon and black pepper into the kwark.
Scatter the sliced spring-onion greens over the tray and serve with the cold dip.
1D3.tip: Spring-onion greens give the onion flavour without the fructans that sit in the white bulb.

1D4.p: Boil the diced potatoes 8 minutes, drain well. Fry them in the oil until crisp at the edges, 10 minutes. Meanwhile bake the fresh mackerel fillet skin-side down at 200 °C for 8–10 minutes, until it flakes. Fold the spinach through the potatoes until wilted, then flake the cooked mackerel over. Top with spring-onion greens; kwark with lemon and black pepper on the side.
s: Boil the diced potatoes 8 minutes, drain well.
Fry them in the oil until crisp at the edges, 10 minutes. Meanwhile bake the fresh mackerel fillet skin-side down at 200 °C for 8–10 minutes, until it flakes.
Fold the spinach through the potatoes until wilted, then flake the cooked mackerel over.
Top with spring-onion greens; kwark with lemon and black pepper on the side.
1D4.tip: Buy fresh mackerel fillets, not smoked — smoked mackerel carries many times the sodium.

1L1.t: Chicken, rice & roast pepper bowl with spinach
1L1.p: Poach the chicken: lower it into a pan of barely simmering water (small bubbles, never a rolling boil), lid on, 12–15 minutes until the thickest part reads 74 °C — or is white right through with clear juices. Gentle heat, not undercooking, is what keeps breast meat juicy. Cook the rice: 1 part rice to 2 parts water, lid on, 25–30 minutes, then rest 5 minutes off the heat. Roast the pepper strips and courgette slices with half the oil at 200 °C for 20 minutes. Wilt the spinach in the hot tray for the last minute. Slice the chicken and assemble the bowl; dress with the remaining oil and lemon, scatter the pumpkin seeds. Amounts are per bowl — on Sunday make three.
s: Poach the chicken: lower it into a pan of barely simmering water (small bubbles, never a rolling boil), lid on, 12–15 minutes until the thickest part reads 74 °C — or is white right through with clear juices. Gentle heat, not undercooking, is what keeps breast meat juicy.
Cook the rice: 1 part rice to 2 parts water, lid on, 25–30 minutes, then rest 5 minutes off the heat.
Roast the pepper strips and courgette slices with half the oil at 200 °C for 20 minutes.
Wilt the spinach in the hot tray for the last minute.
Slice the chicken and assemble the bowl; dress with the remaining oil and lemon, scatter the pumpkin seeds. Amounts are per bowl — on Sunday make three.
1L1.tip: Pepper, spinach and courgette at this portion are among the least gassy vegetables there are.

1L2.t: Tuna, egg & potato salad with kwark-dill dressing
1L2.p: Boil the potatoes (skin on) 15–18 minutes and the egg for 9 minutes; cool both under cold water. Dressing: kwark, lemon juice, a teaspoon of mustard, chopped dill, black pepper and the oil. Cut potatoes, egg, cucumber and tomato into chunks; drain the tuna. Toss everything with the spinach and dressing. Keeps 2 days in the fridge.
s: Boil the potatoes (skin on) 15–18 minutes and the egg for 9 minutes; cool both under cold water.
Dressing: kwark, lemon juice, a teaspoon of mustard, chopped dill, black pepper and the oil.
Cut potatoes, egg, cucumber and tomato into chunks; drain the tuna.
Toss everything with the spinach and dressing. Keeps 2 days in the fridge.
1L2.tip: Cooled potatoes form resistant starch — it feeds gut bacteria but ferments more slowly than bean sugars, so it is usually gentler.

1L3.p: Drain the lentils into a sieve and rinse under the cold tap for 30 seconds. Soften the carrot and parsnip in the oil for 5 minutes with half the sliced spring-onion greens. Add the diced potato, the whole chicken breast and 700 ml water with a bay leaf; simmer 20 minutes. Lift out the chicken, shred it with two forks and return it with the lentils; heat through 3 minutes. Serve with the rest of the spring-onion greens, the slice of rye and a big spoon of cold kwark on top at the table.
s: Drain the lentils into a sieve and rinse under the cold tap for 30 seconds.
Soften the carrot and parsnip in the oil for 5 minutes with half the sliced spring-onion greens.
Add the diced potato, the whole chicken breast and 700 ml water with a bay leaf; simmer 20 minutes.
Lift out the chicken, shred it with two forks and return it with the lentils; heat through 3 minutes.
Serve with the rest of the spring-onion greens, the slice of rye and a big spoon of cold kwark on top at the table.
1L3.tip: A third of a can of lentils per bowl — about two low-FODMAP servings. Rinsing drains away a good share of the gas-forming sugars.

1S1.p: Segment the orange over the kwark, scatter the almonds.
s: Segment the orange over the kwark, scatter the almonds.
1S1.tip: Oranges are one of the gentlest fruits for gas — much easier than apples or pears.

1S2.t: Skyr with kiwi, pumpkin seeds & a glass of kefir
1S2.p: Slice the kiwi over the skyr and add the pumpkin seeds; drink the kefir alongside.
s: Slice the kiwi over the skyr and add the pumpkin seeds; drink the kefir alongside.
1S2.tip: Buy plain skyr — flavoured 0% versions are often sweetened with sucralose or acesulfame-K.

1S3.p: Thaw the blueberries overnight in the fridge, or 1 minute in the microwave; stir through the kwark with the linseed, walnuts on top.
s: Thaw the blueberries overnight in the fridge, or 1 minute in the microwave; stir through the kwark with the linseed, walnuts on top.
1S3.tip: Blueberries rather than a mixed-berry bag: mixed bags usually include blackberries, which are high in sorbitol.

2B1.p: Night before: mix the oats, linseed, kefir and skyr with a pinch of cinnamon. Cover and refrigerate overnight. Morning: slice the banana on top and add the almonds.
s: Night before: mix the oats, linseed, kefir and skyr with a pinch of cinnamon.
Cover and refrigerate overnight.
Morning: slice the banana on top and add the almonds.
2B1.tip: Pick bananas that are still slightly green at the tips — fully ripe, speckled bananas carry far more fructans.

2B2.p: Wilt the spinach in the oil, then pour in the three beaten eggs. Add the tomato wedges when the eggs are almost set, so they don't water the omelette down. Fold once and slide out while still glossy. Rye, cold kwark and a glass of kefir on the side.
s: Wilt the spinach in the oil, then pour in the three beaten eggs.
Add the tomato wedges when the eggs are almost set, so they don't water the omelette down.
Fold once and slide out while still glossy. Rye, cold kwark and a glass of kefir on the side.
2B2.tip: One slice of rye rather than two keeps wheat and rye fructans at a comfortable dose.

2D1.t: Cod traybake with potatoes, aubergine & tomato
2D1.p: Heat the oven to 200 °C. Potatoes in wedges and aubergine in cubes, tossed with the oil and oregano, roast 20 minutes. Add the tomato halves and lay the cod on top; roast 12 more minutes. Lemon over at the end; cold kwark with dill and lemon as the sauce.
s: Heat the oven to 200 °C. Potatoes in wedges and aubergine in cubes, tossed with the oil and oregano, roast 20 minutes.
Add the tomato halves and lay the cod on top; roast 12 more minutes.
Lemon over at the end; cold kwark with dill and lemon as the sauce.
2D1.tip: Aubergine is gentle at a normal side portion like this one; very large servings add sorbitol.

2D2.t: Tempeh chilli with rice & a cold kwark topping
2D2.p: Crumble the tempeh with your fingers. Warm the oil with a lightly crushed garlic clove for 2 minutes on low heat, then lift the clove out — the flavour stays in the oil, the gas-forming fructans don't (they are water-soluble, not oil-soluble). Brown the tempeh in the garlic oil 5 minutes; add the diced carrot and pepper with cumin, smoked paprika powder and chilli flakes, 3 minutes. Add the tomatoes and 100 ml water; simmer 15 minutes. Serve on the rice with a spoon of cold kwark in place of sour cream and the spring-onion greens.
s: Crumble the tempeh with your fingers.

Warm the oil with a lightly crushed garlic clove for 2 minutes on low heat, then lift the clove out — the flavour stays in the oil, the gas-forming fructans don't (they are water-soluble, not oil-soluble).
Brown the tempeh in the garlic oil 5 minutes; add the diced carrot and pepper with cumin, smoked paprika powder and chilli flakes, 3 minutes.
Add the tomatoes and 100 ml water; simmer 15 minutes.
Serve on the rice with a spoon of cold kwark in place of sour cream and the spring-onion greens.
2D2.tip: Tempeh is fermented soy — it gives chilli its meaty bite without the kidney-bean gas load.

2D3.t: Chicken, pak choi & pepper stir-fry with rice
2D3.p: Cook the rice (1:2 water, 25 minutes). Warm the oil with a lightly crushed garlic clove for 2 minutes on low heat, then lift the clove out — the flavour stays in the oil, the gas-forming fructans don't (they are water-soluble, not oil-soluble). Very hot pan: chicken strips 3 minutes, then out. Carrot matchsticks 2 minutes, pepper 2 minutes, pak choi 2 minutes, chicken back in with grated ginger and a splash of vinegar. Serve on the rice, spring-onion greens on top.
s: Cook the rice (1:2 water, 25 minutes).

Warm the oil with a lightly crushed garlic clove for 2 minutes on low heat, then lift the clove out — the flavour stays in the oil, the gas-forming fructans don't (they are water-soluble, not oil-soluble).
Very hot pan: chicken strips 3 minutes, then out.
Carrot matchsticks 2 minutes, pepper 2 minutes, pak choi 2 minutes, chicken back in with grated ginger and a splash of vinegar.
Serve on the rice, spring-onion greens on top.
2D3.tip: Pepper, carrot and pak choi keep a stir-fry gentle. Mangetout is out: the comfortable serve is about five pods, and the old plan used 200 g.

2D4.t: Mackerel with warm potato, beetroot & spinach
2D4.p: Boil the potatoes 15 minutes; bake the fresh mackerel fillet skin-side down at 200 °C for 8–10 minutes, until it flakes. Dice the beetroot. Dressing: kwark, mustard, lemon and dill. Toss the warm potato, beetroot and spinach with the oil; flake the cooked mackerel over, dressing on the side.
s: Boil the potatoes 15 minutes; bake the fresh mackerel fillet skin-side down at 200 °C for 8–10 minutes, until it flakes. Dice the beetroot.
Dressing: kwark, mustard, lemon and dill.
Toss the warm potato, beetroot and spinach with the oil; flake the cooked mackerel over, dressing on the side.
2D4.tip: Beetroot is kept to a small handful — at 200 g it's a notable source of fructans and GOS.

2L1.t: Chicken & buckwheat bowl with roast courgette & pepper
2L1.p: Poach the chicken: lower it into a pan of barely simmering water (small bubbles, never a rolling boil), lid on, 12–15 minutes until the thickest part reads 74 °C — or is white right through with clear juices. Gentle heat, not undercooking, is what keeps breast meat juicy. Buckwheat: rinse, then simmer in twice its volume of water for 12–15 minutes; leave covered 5 minutes. Roast courgette and pepper with half the oil at 200 °C for 20 minutes. Massage the shredded kale with the rest of the oil and lemon. Assemble the bowl: buckwheat, vegetables, sliced chicken, kale, pumpkin seeds. Amounts are per bowl — on Sunday make three.
s: Poach the chicken: lower it into a pan of barely simmering water (small bubbles, never a rolling boil), lid on, 12–15 minutes until the thickest part reads 74 °C — or is white right through with clear juices. Gentle heat, not undercooking, is what keeps breast meat juicy.
Buckwheat: rinse, then simmer in twice its volume of water for 12–15 minutes; leave covered 5 minutes.
Roast courgette and pepper with half the oil at 200 °C for 20 minutes.
Massage the shredded kale with the rest of the oil and lemon.
Assemble the bowl: buckwheat, vegetables, sliced chicken, kale, pumpkin seeds. Amounts are per bowl — on Sunday make three.
2L1.tip: Buckwheat (grechka) is gluten-free and low in fructans, so it's a gentler grain than bulgur or couscous.

2L2.p: Rinse the chickpeas under the cold tap for 30 seconds and drain well. Boil the potatoes 15–18 minutes and cool. Dressing: kwark, lemon, mustard, chopped parsley, black pepper, the oil. Combine tuna, chickpeas, potato, cucumber, tomato and spring-onion greens; dress.
s: Rinse the chickpeas under the cold tap for 30 seconds and drain well.
Boil the potatoes 15–18 minutes and cool.
Dressing: kwark, lemon, mustard, chopped parsley, black pepper, the oil.
Combine tuna, chickpeas, potato, cucumber, tomato and spring-onion greens; dress.
2L2.tip: 80 g of chickpeas is a third of a can — enough for fibre and flavour, less than half of what the old salad used.

2L3.t: Tomato, lentil & pepper soup with chicken
2L3.p: Rinse the lentils in a sieve for 30 seconds. Soften the diced carrot and pepper in the oil with smoked paprika powder and cumin, 5 minutes. Add the diced potato, the tomatoes, the whole chicken breast and 600 ml water; simmer 20 minutes. Shred the chicken, return it with the lentils, heat 3 minutes. Blend half if you like it thicker. Serve with rye and a spoon of cold kwark on top.
s: Rinse the lentils in a sieve for 30 seconds.
Soften the diced carrot and pepper in the oil with smoked paprika powder and cumin, 5 minutes.
Add the diced potato, the tomatoes, the whole chicken breast and 600 ml water; simmer 20 minutes.
Shred the chicken, return it with the lentils, heat 3 minutes. Blend half if you like it thicker.
Serve with rye and a spoon of cold kwark on top.
2L3.tip: Cumin and ginger are traditional carminatives — small doses in every legume dish are worth the habit.

2S1.p: Slice the kiwi over the skyr, walnuts on top.
s: Slice the kiwi over the skyr, walnuts on top.
2S1.tip: Kiwifruit is one of the foods the British Dietetic Association's 2025 constipation guideline supports.

2S2.p: Loosen the peanut butter with a spoon of water so it stirs through the kwark; add the linseed and slice the banana on top.
s: Loosen the peanut butter with a spoon of water so it stirs through the kwark; add the linseed and slice the banana on top.
2S2.tip: Peanuts are legumes but low in GOS — peanut butter rarely causes the gas that beans do.

2S3.p: Stir the thawed blueberries through the kwark, walnuts on top.
s: Stir the thawed blueberries through the kwark, walnuts on top.
2S3.tip: Walnuts are one of the best-tolerated nuts at a small handful.

3B1.t: Kefir overnight oats with blueberries & walnuts
3B1.p: Night before: stir oats and linseed into the kefir and kwark with cinnamon; refrigerate. Morning: top with the thawed blueberries and walnuts.
s: Night before: stir oats and linseed into the kefir and kwark with cinnamon; refrigerate.
Morning: top with the thawed blueberries and walnuts.
3B1.tip: Same base as Week 1 with blueberries — plain dairy, no sweetener needed.

3B2.p: Warm the oil with a lightly crushed garlic clove for 2 minutes on low heat, then lift the clove out — the flavour stays in the oil, the gas-forming fructans don't (they are water-soluble, not oil-soluble). Simmer the tomatoes in the garlic oil with paprika powder and cumin for 5 minutes until thickened; wilt the spinach through. Make three hollows and crack an egg into each; lid on, low heat, 6–7 minutes until the whites set. Rye, cold kwark and a glass of kefir on the side.
s: Warm the oil with a lightly crushed garlic clove for 2 minutes on low heat, then lift the clove out — the flavour stays in the oil, the gas-forming fructans don't (they are water-soluble, not oil-soluble).
Simmer the tomatoes in the garlic oil with paprika powder and cumin for 5 minutes until thickened; wilt the spinach through.
Make three hollows and crack an egg into each; lid on, low heat, 6–7 minutes until the whites set.
Rye, cold kwark and a glass of kefir on the side.
3B2.tip: A shakshuka without the onion: garlic oil and cumin carry it.

3D1.p: Boil the potato and parsnip together 15–18 minutes; mash with half the oil, nutmeg and black pepper. Bake the salmon at 200 °C for 12–14 minutes. Wilt the spinach in the pan with the remaining oil. Lemon over the fish.
s: Boil the potato and parsnip together 15–18 minutes; mash with half the oil, nutmeg and black pepper.
Bake the salmon at 200 °C for 12–14 minutes.
Wilt the spinach in the pan with the remaining oil. Lemon over the fish.
3D1.tip: Parsnip replaces the old cauliflower mash: it's sweet, fibre-rich and has no FODMAP limit at normal portions.

3D2.t: Tempeh, pak choi & carrot stir-fry with rice
3D2.p: Cut the tempeh into thin slices. Cook the rice (1:2 water, 25 minutes). Warm the oil with a lightly crushed garlic clove for 2 minutes on low heat, then lift the clove out — the flavour stays in the oil, the gas-forming fructans don't (they are water-soluble, not oil-soluble). Fry the tempeh until golden on both sides, 5 minutes; lift out. Stir-fry carrot and pepper 3 minutes, pak choi 2 minutes; tempeh back in with grated ginger and a splash of vinegar. Serve on the rice with spring-onion greens.
s: Cut the tempeh into thin slices. Cook the rice (1:2 water, 25 minutes).

Warm the oil with a lightly crushed garlic clove for 2 minutes on low heat, then lift the clove out — the flavour stays in the oil, the gas-forming fructans don't (they are water-soluble, not oil-soluble).
Fry the tempeh until golden on both sides, 5 minutes; lift out.
Stir-fry carrot and pepper 3 minutes, pak choi 2 minutes; tempeh back in with grated ginger and a splash of vinegar.
Serve on the rice with spring-onion greens.
3D2.tip: Up to about 170 g, tempeh counts as low-FODMAP — fermentation breaks down much of the soy's gas-forming sugar.

3D3.t: Turkey kotlety in tomato sauce with buckwheat
3D3.p: Panade: soak the oats in the kwark for 10 minutes. Mix with the mince, the grated and squeezed courgette, finely sliced spring-onion greens, beaten egg and black pepper. Chill 20 minutes, then shape 5 kotlety. Simmer the tomatoes with the oil and paprika powder 5 minutes, lay the kotlety in, lid on, 14–16 minutes until 74 °C in the centre — no frying. Wilt the spinach into the sauce for the last minute; serve on buckwheat (rinse, simmer 12–15 minutes in twice its volume of water).
s: Panade: soak the oats in the kwark for 10 minutes.
Mix with the mince, the grated and squeezed courgette, finely sliced spring-onion greens, beaten egg and black pepper.
Chill 20 minutes, then shape 5 kotlety.
Simmer the tomatoes with the oil and paprika powder 5 minutes, lay the kotlety in, lid on, 14–16 minutes until 74 °C in the centre — no frying.
Wilt the spinach into the sauce for the last minute; serve on buckwheat (rinse, simmer 12–15 minutes in twice its volume of water).
3D3.tip: Buy plain ('ongekruid') mince — seasoned turkey or chicken mince can carry four times the sodium.

3D4.t: Chicken plov with carrot, cumin & cucumber salad
3D4.p: Warm the oil with a lightly crushed garlic clove for 2 minutes on low heat, then lift the clove out — the flavour stays in the oil, the gas-forming fructans don't (they are water-soluble, not oil-soluble). Brown the diced chicken breast in the garlic oil for 3 minutes and lift it out. Add the carrot cut into matchsticks and a teaspoon of cumin seeds; cook 5 minutes. Add the rinsed rice and 150 ml boiling water, lid on, lowest heat. After 18 minutes lay the chicken on top, lid back on, 12 more minutes — don't stir. Fluff with a fork, scatter spring-onion greens. Cucumber and tomato with the cold kwark and dill on the side.
s: Warm the oil with a lightly crushed garlic clove for 2 minutes on low heat, then lift the clove out — the flavour stays in the oil, the gas-forming fructans don't (they are water-soluble, not oil-soluble).
Brown the diced chicken breast in the garlic oil for 3 minutes and lift it out.
Add the carrot cut into matchsticks and a teaspoon of cumin seeds; cook 5 minutes.
Add the rinsed rice and 150 ml boiling water, lid on, lowest heat. After 18 minutes lay the chicken on top, lid back on, 12 more minutes — don't stir.
Fluff with a fork, scatter spring-onion greens. Cucumber and tomato with the cold kwark and dill on the side.
3D4.tip: Classic plov uses a lot of onion; this keeps the cumin and carrot sweetness that actually make it plov.

3L1.t: Chicken, buckwheat & roast pumpkin bowl with kale
3L1.p: Poach the chicken: lower it into a pan of barely simmering water (small bubbles, never a rolling boil), lid on, 12–15 minutes until the thickest part reads 74 °C — or is white right through with clear juices. Gentle heat, not undercooking, is what keeps breast meat juicy. Roast the Hokkaido pumpkin cubes (skin on is fine) and pepper strips with half the oil at 200 °C for 25 minutes. Buckwheat: rinse, simmer in twice its volume of water 12–15 minutes, rest covered 5 minutes. Massage the kale with the remaining oil and lemon until it softens. Assemble the bowl and scatter the pumpkin seeds. Amounts are per bowl — on Sunday make three.
s: Poach the chicken: lower it into a pan of barely simmering water (small bubbles, never a rolling boil), lid on, 12–15 minutes until the thickest part reads 74 °C — or is white right through with clear juices. Gentle heat, not undercooking, is what keeps breast meat juicy.
Roast the Hokkaido pumpkin cubes (skin on is fine) and pepper strips with half the oil at 200 °C for 25 minutes.
Buckwheat: rinse, simmer in twice its volume of water 12–15 minutes, rest covered 5 minutes.
Massage the kale with the remaining oil and lemon until it softens.
Assemble the bowl and scatter the pumpkin seeds. Amounts are per bowl — on Sunday make three.
3L1.tip: Hokkaido pumpkin at about 100 g per bowl is gentler than butternut, which adds fructans in larger servings.

3L2.p: Rinse the beans for 30 seconds and drain. Boil the potatoes 15–18 minutes and cool. Dressing: kwark, lemon, plenty of chopped dill, black pepper and the oil. Combine tuna, beans, potatoes, cucumber, tomato and spring-onion greens; dress.
s: Rinse the beans for 30 seconds and drain.
Boil the potatoes 15–18 minutes and cool.
Dressing: kwark, lemon, plenty of chopped dill, black pepper and the oil.
Combine tuna, beans, potatoes, cucumber, tomato and spring-onion greens; dress.
3L2.tip: If this sits well, you can try 120 g of beans next time — raise one legume at a time.

3L3.t: Spiced carrot, pumpkin & lentil soup with chicken
3L3.p: Rinse the lentils for 30 seconds. Soften the sliced carrot and cubed pumpkin in the oil with cumin, grated ginger and a pinch of chilli, 5 minutes. Add the diced potato, the tomatoes, the whole chicken breast and 700 ml water; simmer 20 minutes. Shred the chicken; blend the soup until smooth, return chicken and lentils, heat 3 minutes. Rye on the side, cold kwark on top.
s: Rinse the lentils for 30 seconds.
Soften the sliced carrot and cubed pumpkin in the oil with cumin, grated ginger and a pinch of chilli, 5 minutes.
Add the diced potato, the tomatoes, the whole chicken breast and 700 ml water; simmer 20 minutes.
Shred the chicken; blend the soup until smooth, return chicken and lentils, heat 3 minutes.
Rye on the side, cold kwark on top.
3L3.tip: Blending doesn't reduce the fermentable sugars, but the small lentil portion does.

3S1.p: Segment the orange over the kwark, scatter the almonds.
s: Segment the orange over the kwark, scatter the almonds.

3S2.p: Slice the kiwi over the skyr, add the pumpkin seeds and linseed.
s: Slice the kiwi over the skyr, add the pumpkin seeds and linseed.
3S2.tip: One kiwi a day is a gentle start; the constipation guideline used two to three.

3S3.p: Segment the orange over the kwark, walnuts on top.
s: Segment the orange over the kwark, walnuts on top.
3S3.tip: Walnuts: good omega-3 for very little gas.

4B1.t: Kefir oats with banana & peanut butter
4B1.p: Night before: oats, linseed, kefir and kwark in a box; refrigerate. Morning: slice the banana on top and loosen the peanut butter over it with a drop of water.
s: Night before: oats, linseed, kefir and kwark in a box; refrigerate.
Morning: slice the banana on top and loosen the peanut butter over it with a drop of water.
4B1.tip: Firm, slightly green bananas are the gentle ones.

4B2.p: Wilt the spinach in the oil, pour over the beaten eggs. Tomato in at the end so it doesn't water the eggs down; fold once, off the heat while still glossy. Rye, cold kwark and a glass of kefir on the side.
s: Wilt the spinach in the oil, pour over the beaten eggs.
Tomato in at the end so it doesn't water the eggs down; fold once, off the heat while still glossy.
Rye, cold kwark and a glass of kefir on the side.
4B2.tip: Three eggs, kwark and kefir put breakfast protein near 50 g.

4D1.p: Heat the oven to 200 °C. Potato wedges and fennel wedges with the oil, 20 minutes. Add the courgette rounds and salmon; 12–14 more minutes. Lemon and dill to finish.
s: Heat the oven to 200 °C. Potato wedges and fennel wedges with the oil, 20 minutes.
Add the courgette rounds and salmon; 12–14 more minutes.
Lemon and dill to finish.
4D1.tip: One tray, one dish to wash.

4D2.t: Tofu stir-fry with pak choi, pepper & rice
4D2.p: Press the tofu 20 minutes, then cube. Cook the rice. Warm the oil with a lightly crushed garlic clove for 2 minutes on low heat, then lift the clove out — the flavour stays in the oil, the gas-forming fructans don't (they are water-soluble, not oil-soluble). Fry the tofu until coloured on all sides, 6–8 minutes; lift out. Carrot and pepper 3 minutes, pak choi 2 minutes, tofu back in with ginger and a splash of vinegar. Serve on the rice with spring-onion greens.
s: Press the tofu 20 minutes, then cube. Cook the rice.

Warm the oil with a lightly crushed garlic clove for 2 minutes on low heat, then lift the clove out — the flavour stays in the oil, the gas-forming fructans don't (they are water-soluble, not oil-soluble).
Fry the tofu until coloured on all sides, 6–8 minutes; lift out.
Carrot and pepper 3 minutes, pak choi 2 minutes, tofu back in with ginger and a splash of vinegar.
Serve on the rice with spring-onion greens.
4D2.tip: No soy sauce: it's a big sodium hit, and vinegar plus ginger does the job.

4D3.p: Heat the oven to 200 °C. Parsnip, potato and carrot in chunks with most of the oil and paprika powder; roast 15 minutes. Add the chicken breast in large chunks, tossed in the rest of the oil; roast 18–20 minutes more, adding the kale for the last 5 so it crisps. Cold kwark with lemon, dill and black pepper as a dip.
s: Heat the oven to 200 °C. Parsnip, potato and carrot in chunks with most of the oil and paprika powder; roast 15 minutes.
Add the chicken breast in large chunks, tossed in the rest of the oil; roast 18–20 minutes more, adding the kale for the last 5 so it crisps.
Cold kwark with lemon, dill and black pepper as a dip.
4D3.tip: Parsnip has no FODMAP limit at normal portions — it takes over from sweet potato, which adds fructans in larger servings.

4D4.p: Boil the potatoes 15 minutes; bake the fresh mackerel fillet skin-side down at 200 °C for 8–10 minutes, until it flakes. Dice the beetroot and cucumber. Kwark, mustard and dill dressing. Toss the warm potatoes with the beetroot, cucumber and oil; flake the cooked mackerel on top.
s: Boil the potatoes 15 minutes; bake the fresh mackerel fillet skin-side down at 200 °C for 8–10 minutes, until it flakes. Dice the beetroot and cucumber.
Kwark, mustard and dill dressing.
Toss the warm potatoes with the beetroot, cucumber and oil; flake the cooked mackerel on top.
4D4.tip: Small beetroot portion, same colour and flavour.

4L1.p: Poach the chicken: lower it into a pan of barely simmering water (small bubbles, never a rolling boil), lid on, 12–15 minutes until the thickest part reads 74 °C — or is white right through with clear juices. Gentle heat, not undercooking, is what keeps breast meat juicy. Cook the rice (1:2 water, 25–30 minutes). Roast pepper, courgette and carrot with half the oil at 200 °C for 20 minutes. Assemble the bowl, dress with the remaining oil and lemon, scatter pumpkin seeds. Amounts are per bowl — on Sunday make three.
s: Poach the chicken: lower it into a pan of barely simmering water (small bubbles, never a rolling boil), lid on, 12–15 minutes until the thickest part reads 74 °C — or is white right through with clear juices. Gentle heat, not undercooking, is what keeps breast meat juicy.
Cook the rice (1:2 water, 25–30 minutes).
Roast pepper, courgette and carrot with half the oil at 200 °C for 20 minutes.
Assemble the bowl, dress with the remaining oil and lemon, scatter pumpkin seeds. Amounts are per bowl — on Sunday make three.
4L1.tip: Rice replaces couscous here — wheat couscous is a fructan source, rice has none.

4L2.t: Chicken, egg & chickpea salad with mustard dressing
4L2.p: Poach the chicken as for the bowls (bare simmer, 74 °C in the centre), boil the egg 9 minutes and the potatoes 15–18 minutes; cool. Rinse the chickpeas for 30 seconds and drain. Dressing: kwark, a teaspoon of mustard, lemon, black pepper and the oil. Slice the chicken; cut the potatoes, cucumber and tomato into chunks; toss everything with the spinach and dressing, halve the egg on top.
s: Poach the chicken as for the bowls (bare simmer, 74 °C in the centre), boil the egg 9 minutes and the potatoes 15–18 minutes; cool.
Rinse the chickpeas for 30 seconds and drain.
Dressing: kwark, a teaspoon of mustard, lemon, black pepper and the oil.
Slice the chicken; cut the potatoes, cucumber and tomato into chunks; toss everything with the spinach and dressing, halve the egg on top.
4L2.tip: Chickpeas stay at a third of a can per meal — never two legume meals on the same day.

4L3.t: Ukha — Russian fish soup with cod, potato & dill
4L3.p: Simmer half the sliced spring-onion greens with the carrot, parsnip and diced potato in 800 ml water with a bay leaf and a few peppercorns, 15 minutes. Add the cod in large chunks; poach 6–8 minutes without boiling hard. Finish with a handful of chopped dill, the rest of the spring-onion greens, lemon and the oil. Rye on the side, cold kwark to spoon in.
s: Simmer half the sliced spring-onion greens with the carrot, parsnip and diced potato in 800 ml water with a bay leaf and a few peppercorns, 15 minutes.
Add the cod in large chunks; poach 6–8 minutes without boiling hard.
Finish with a handful of chopped dill, the rest of the spring-onion greens, lemon and the oil.
Rye on the side, cold kwark to spoon in.
4L3.tip: Ukha is naturally gentle: fish, roots and dill, no beans, no onion needed.

4S1.p: Slice the kiwi over the kwark, walnuts on top.
s: Slice the kiwi over the kwark, walnuts on top.

4S2.p: Segment the orange over the skyr, almonds on top.
s: Segment the orange over the skyr, almonds on top.
4S2.tip: Citrus is low-FODMAP at a normal fruit portion.

4S3.p: Segment the orange over the kwark, pumpkin seeds on top.
s: Segment the orange over the kwark, pumpkin seeds on top.
4S3.tip: Seeds add magnesium and plant variety for very few grams.

1.c: Calm start — lowest legume dose, soups and bowls on potato and rice
prep: Shopping day: freeze any raw meat or fish you won't cook within two days (mince within one), and move each pack to the fridge the night before you need it.

Sunday — lunch bowls: poach 480 g chicken, cook 195 g rice (dry weight), roast 450 g pepper, 180 g courgette. Box three: Monday and Tuesday in the fridge, Friday's in the freezer — move it to the fridge Thursday night.
Wednesday and Saturday evening — salads: boil 200 g potatoes and an egg for the next day's lunch (Thursday, Sunday).
Wednesday — soup: cook the chicken, lentil & root vegetable soup double and freeze Saturday's bowl straight away; thaw it in the fridge Friday night.
Tofu days (Tuesday, Friday) — press the tofu in the fridge that morning, between two plates with a weight on top; it's a 15-minute cook in the evening.
Night before Monday, Wednesday, Friday and Sunday — fill the overnight-oats jar; two minutes.
flavour: Sauce Sunday: tahini-lemon drizzle (freeze Friday's portion), green sauce for the salmon, quick pickles, chilli crunch. Tuesday: peanut-lime sauce for the tofu nights.

prep: Shopping day: freeze any raw meat or fish you won't cook within two days (mince within one), and move each pack to the fridge the night before you need it.

Pinch-size extras, optional: ground coriander (AH Verstegen 33 g €3.09), cardamom (32 g €5.69), five-spice (75 g €5.19), turmeric. Skip them or use cumin and cinnamon instead.
